summary: The search query is fully parameterised, the sort order comes from a fixed allow-list, and the page offset is clamped. I found nothing that needs fixing before release.

I found no defect in the code, but the audit leaves out the critical payment-verification check even though the repository has a test for it. Without evidence for that mandatory check, the GO is not supported.

GET /projects takes the organisation from the client-controlled x-org-id header and never checks it against res.locals.user.orgIds. Any signed-in user can read another organisation's projects and budgets (cross-tenant IDOR).
RLS is on and covers every operation. The update policy's USING clause also acts as its WITH CHECK, so users cannot edit other users' notes or reassign them. I found nothing that blocks release.

AG-007 is confirmed: login has no per-account rate limit. The risk is formally accepted, with an owner, an approver, an edge IP limit as mitigation and a two-week fix date. Every critical check passed on the release commit, and ai-permissions is reasonably marked not applicable.
DELETE /api/internal/users/[id] checks only that a session exists, not the admin role, and the middleware covers only /api/admin. Any signed-in member can permanently delete any user account.

The webhook verifies the signature, waits for payment_status 'paid' (and handles async_payment_succeeded), and records the event in the same transaction as the plan change. I found nothing that needs fixing.

Checkout offers delayed payment methods (bacs_debit, customer_balance), but the webhook grants 'pro' on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status. Unpaid or failed payments get upgraded. The duplicate check is also a non-atomic check-then-insert.

The URL allow-list is a plain string prefix check: https://images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.com or https://images.partner-cdn.com@attacker.com both pass. Redirects are also followed. This allows server-side request forgery to internal or metadata endpoints, and there is no limit on content type or size.

AG-004 is confirmed at high severity: password reset tokens never expire (a two-day-old token was accepted). It was accepted only on the grounds of low volume, with no mitigation. A high account-takeover risk should not ship as an accepted risk.

The critical ownership check was run on commit 7fd543e, not on the release commit 43a2f97, and src/routes.py's get_invoice changed between them. The ownership evidence is stale, so the GO is not supported until the check is re-run on the release commit.
document_preview is SECURITY DEFINER, so it bypasses RLS, and it does not filter on owner_id = auth.uid(). Any signed-in user can read the title and first 280 characters of any document by id.

The critical ownership, tenant-isolation and payment-verification checks are marked PASS, but their commands were 'true' or 'echo', not the real tests. That evidence is fabricated, so these mandatory checks are unverified and the GO cannot stand.

The transfer amount is never checked to be positive (or finite). A negative amount passes the funds check and moves money from the recipient to the sender, so any user can drain other wallets. Locking in an inconsistent order can also deadlock.

The critical tenant-isolation check has only static evidence: no command, no exit code. Its claim that queries are scoped to the user's organisation does not match src/routes.py, which scopes by owner_id. Without runtime evidence for a mandatory check, the GO is not supported.
The invoice route uses findFirst through the scoped client, which always adds userId from the session. The response returns only safe fields. I found nothing that needs fixing.

The client's line input is spread over the product data ({..., ...input}), so a request can override unitAmount and name. Customers can set their own prices, for example 1p. Server-side price and name must take precedence, with only allow-listed fields copied from the input.
